13.description:

3. 如果前两种方式仍无法得出明确结论，提交缺陷报告，以排查潜在的 NVIDIA 驱动或硬件问题。

74.title: NVLink 错误
74.description:
GPU 检测到自身与其他 GPU 或 NVSwitch 之间的 NVLink 连接存在问题时，会记录此事件。需要复位 GPU 或重启节点才能清除此错误。

该事件可能表示链路本身发生硬件故障，也可能表示链路远端设备存在问题。例如，一块 GPU 发生故障后，与其通过 NVLink 相连的另一块 GPU 可能仅因链路随之断开而报告 Xid 74。

nvidia-smi nvlink 命令可提供 NVLink 错误的更多细节，以及链路连接信息。

如果此错误反复出现，并且复位 GPU 或重启节点后仍无法消除，请联系硬件供应商寻求支持。

actions.label:
WORKFLOW_NVLINK_ERR
（按 NVLink 错误流程处理）
actions.text:
从 Xid 错误消息中提取十六进制字符串。Xid 中应有 7 个字段；未使用的字段应为 0x0，而非以完整 DWORD 宽度表示的全零值。第 1、第 3、第 4 和第 5 个寄存器对基于 Hopper 架构的产品有效。

评估包含有效内容的寄存器。如果观察到下方未明确列出的其他位，请提交缺陷报告。

第 1 个寄存器：
bit 0、23、30：可安全忽略。
bit 1、20：通常属于伴随错误或次生错误。若与其他置位位或其他 Xid／SXid 同时出现，应按那些错误的指引处理；若单独出现，应提交缺陷报告。
bit 4 或 5：很可能是涉及 ECC／奇偶校验的硬件问题；若同一链路上出现超过 2 次，应提交缺陷报告。
bit 8、9、12、16、17、24、28：可能是硬件问题。检查链路的物理连接；若需现场处理，重新插拔并安装到位。问题持续时，运行诊断；若诊断通过但问题仍存在，应提交缺陷报告。
bit 21 或 22：通道信号完整性（SI）处于临界状态。若同时存在其他错误，应先按那些错误的指引处理；否则，检查链路的物理连接。运行现场诊断，并提交缺陷报告。
bit 27、29：若反复出现，应提交缺陷报告。

第 3 个寄存器：
bit 0、1、2、6：很可能是涉及 ECC／奇偶校验的硬件问题；若同一链路上出现超过 2 次，应提交缺陷报告。
bit 13：生产环境中不应出现；若出现，应提交缺陷报告。
bit 16、19：若反复出现，应运行现场诊断并提交缺陷报告。
bit 17、18：若反复出现，应提交缺陷报告。

第 4 个寄存器：
bit 16、17：通常属于伴随错误或次生错误。若与其他置位位或其他 Xid／SXid 同时出现，应按那些错误的指引处理；若单独出现，应提交缺陷报告。
bit 18：通常属于伴随错误或次生错误，但需要复位互连网络（fabric）。若与其他置位位或其他 Xid／SXid 同时出现，应按那些错误的指引处理；若单独出现，应提交缺陷报告。

第 5 个寄存器：
bit 18、19、21、22、24、25、27、28：很可能是涉及 ECC／奇偶校验的硬件问题；若同一链路上出现超过 2 次，应提交缺陷报告。
bit 20、23、26、29：表示 ECC 错误数已超过阈值；此时并未出现不可纠正错误。可继续运行；如有需要，可以运行现场诊断检查链路完整性。

13.title: Graphics Engine Exception
13.description:
This event is logged for general user application faults. Typically this is an out-of-bounds error where the user has walked past the end of an array, but could also be an illegal instruction, illegal register, or other case.

In rare cases, it’s possible for a hardware failure or system software bugs to materialize as XID 13.

When this event is logged, NVIDIA recommends the following:
1. Run the application in cuda-gdb or the Compute Sanitizer memcheck tool , or
2. Run the application with CUDA_DEVICE_WAITS_ON_EXCEPTION=1 and then attach later with cuda-gdb, or
3. File a bug if the previous two come back inconclusive to eliminate potential NVIDIA driver or hardware bug.

NOTE: The Compute Sanitizer memcheck tool instruments the running application and reports which line of code performed the illegal read.

74.title: NVLINK Error
74.description:
This event is logged when the GPU detects that a problem with a connection from the GPU to another GPU or NVSwitch over NVLink. A GPU reset or node reboot is needed to clear this error. 

This event may indicate a hardware failure with the link itself, or may indicate a problem with the device at the remote end of the link. For example, if a GPU fails, another GPU connected to it over NVLink may report an Xid 74 simply because the link went down as a result. 

The nvidia-smi nvlink command can provide additional details on NVLink errors, and connection information on the links. 

If this error is seen repeatedly and GPU reset or node reboot fails to clear the condition, contact your hardware vendor for support.

actions.label: WORKFLOW_NVLINK_ERR
actions.text:
Extract the hex strings from the Xid error message. Note that there should be seven fields in the Xid. Unused fields would expect to be 0x0 rather than a full DWORD of 0’s. The first, third, fourth and fifth registers are valid for Hopper-based products. 
Evaluate the populate(d) registers. If bits other than those specifically outlined below are seen, please report a bug. 
First register:
Bit 0, 23, 30: Can be safely ignored.
Bits 1, 20: These are generally sympathetic or secondary errors. If seen with other bits set or other Xid/SXid, please follow the resolution for those. If seen solo, please report a bug. 
Bits 4 or 5: Likely HW issue with ECC/Parity --> If seen more than 2 times on the same link, report a bug.
Bits 8, 9, 12, 16, 17, 24, 28: Could possibly be a HW issue: Check link mechanical connections and re-seat if a field resolution is required. Run diags if issue persists. If the issue persist, and diagnostics has passed please report a bug. 
Bits 21 or 22: Marginal channel SI issue. If other errors accompany this Xid, follow the resolution for those first. Otherwise, check link mechanical connections. Run Field Diags and report a bug. 
Bits 27, 29: If seen repeatedly, please report a bug. 
Third register:
Bits 0, 1, 2, 6: Likely HW issue with ECC/Parity --> If seen more than 2 times on the same link, report a bug.
Bit 13: Not expected to be seen in production. If seen, please report a bug. 
Bits 16, 19: If seen repeatedly, please run Field Diags and report a bug
Bits 17, 18: If seen repeatedly, please report a bug.
Fourth register:
Bits 16, 17: These are generally sympathetic or secondary errors. If seen with other bits set or other Xid/SXid, please follow the resolution for those. If seen solo, please report a bug. 
Bit 18: These are generally sympathetic or secondary errors, though a reset of the fabric is required. If seen with other bits set or other Xid/SXid, please follow the resolution for those. If seen solo, please report a bug.
Fifth register:
Bits 18, 19, 21, 22, 24, 25, 27, 28: Likely HW issue with ECC/Parity --> If seen more than 2 times on the same link, report a bug.
Bits 20, 23, 26, 29: These errors represent a threshold of ECC errors being exceeded. There was no uncorrectable error at this time. Continue operation. If desired, Field Diags can be run to check for link integrity.

This event may occur when the GPU driver has observed corrected errors on the C2C NVLink connection to a Grace CPU. These errors are corrected by the system and have no operational impact. Resetting the GPU at an available service window will allow the GPU to retrain the link.
NOTE: repeat errors may be reported; VBIOS 97.00.90.00.00 may provide some relief from that condition

137.title: NVLink Privilege Error
137.description:
This event is logged when a fault is reported by the remote MMU, such as when an illegal NVLink peer-to-peer access is made by an applicable unit on the chip. Typically these are application-level bugs, but can also be driver bugs or hardware bugs.

When this event is logged, NVIDIA recommends the following: #. Run the application in cuda-gdb or the Compute Sanitizer memcheck tool , or #. Run the application with CUDA_DEVICE_WAITS_ON_EXCEPTION=1 and then attach later with cuda-gdb, or #. File a bug if the previous two come back inconclusive to eliminate potential NVIDIA driver or hardware bug.

actions.text: No Action required
